title: companion.json
description: A Laching companion app's facts for tools/*: names, paths (relative to the file), languages and the tool settings. tools/companion.py validates it with the subset of JSON Schema used here (type, required, properties, additionalProperties, items, enum, pattern, minItems).

name.description: Short lowercase name (repo, keychain and log prefixes).

displayName.description: The app's name as users see it.

character.description: The character's name, used in comments and review pages.

tag.description: The Laching release the app pins everywhere.

projectSpec.description: The XcodeGen spec, relative to mac.dir.

iosScheme.description: The iPhone and iPad app's scheme, when the project has one: `l10n.py sync` builds it too (for the iOS Simulator), so strings only it shows aren't marked stale.

app.description: The app target's folder, relative to mac.dir.

core.description: The core Swift package's folder, relative to mac.dir; an app without one leaves it out.

tests.description: The app's test target folder, relative to mac.dir.

devAppName.description: The Debug app's name (install-dev, dev icon).

screenshotEnv.description: The environment variable that starts a screenshot run.

appTests.description: The WinUI app's model tests (net10.0, any OS), under dir; verify.sh runs them when the app or they change.

assets.description: windows/assets.py: the MSIX logos and AppIcon.ico from the app icon.

source.description: A square PNG: the Mac's 1024-pixel app icon.

devSource.description: The DEV-banded icon, for the Debug build's Dev/AppIcon.ico.

screenshots.description: Where windows/screenshots.ps1 copies the shots, e.g. screenshots/windows.

release.description: windows/store-release.ps1 and the windows-release.yml workflow: the Store packages and their bundle.

platforms.description: The packages built and bundled; x64 and ARM64 by default.

bundle.description: The bundle's file name before _<version>_x64_arm64.msixbundle; the app's executable name by default.

android.description: The Android app (Kotlin), a Gradle build that includes Laching's kotlin/ (includeBuild). Absent for an app without one.

core.description: The pure Kotlin module, vector-tested (core by default).

applicationId.description: The Play application id; bundleId by default.

devApplicationId.description: The Debug build's application id; devBundleId by default.

strings.description: Where l10n.py export-android writes values*/strings.xml and xml/locales_config.xml: the app module's res folder.

all.description: Every language the app ships, the source included.

landing.description: The landing page's i18n folder (<lang>.json, languages.ts).

glossaryKeys.description: Catalog keys whose translations work files repeat as a glossary.

glossarySources.description: More glossary keys, read from the app's code: every match of `pattern`'s one group in `file` (relative to the root), such as the names in a catalog of items.

pattern.description: A Python regular expression with one group: the catalog key.

keepNames.description: Names translators keep as they are.

rulesFile.description: Markdown with the app's transcreation rules, sent with every work file.

linuxPo.description: Where export-linux writes <lang>.po, or null for no Linux port.

androidStrings.description: The older name of android.strings (where export-android writes), kept as an alias; android.strings wins when both are set.

stringsdataFilter.description: A path fragment the app's .stringsdata files contain (default <mac.scheme>.build).

phraseComment.description: The translator comment of a phrase key: {character}, {tags}, {flavor}, {flavorNote}, {part}.

flavorNotes.description: Flavor id → what it does for the listener.

writeFlag.description: The environment variable that makes the Swift tests write the vectors.

corePackagePath.description: The Swift package whose tests generate the vectors.

design.description: The folder of skin folders (<skin>/<skin>.rig.json); character.py compiles each.

swiftOut.description: The folder that gets <Skin>Art.swift for each skin (it imports LachingCompanion).

swiftModule.description: The app module those Swift files are compiled into, for reference.

assets.description: Raster: the asset catalog folder that gets an imageset per layer.

windowsAssets.description: Raster: the folder that gets the scale-200/300 PNGs.

moods.description: The Mood cases in order (default: the package's seven).

dir.description: The voices checkout (a submodule holding Voice/).

config.description: voice-config.json: the voice settings per language and voice.

reviewColors.description: The review pages' colors, per scheme: token (paper, card, ink, ink-soft, line, accent, accent-soft, on-accent, done, done-soft, flag, flag-soft, link) → #RRGGBB. Unset tokens keep the defaults.

siteCopyright.description: The rights sentence on the review site, after "Shared with friends who help review <character>'s voice." (default: © displayName, all rights reserved).

copyrightHolder.description: Who holds the copyright in the voices repository's LICENSE line, e.g. "2026 Jane Doe" (default: displayName).

extraClips.description: Clip id → source text of clips that aren't phrases.

required.description: Clip ids every voiced language must have before shipping.

recipes.description: A Python module defining sounds(engine) → {name: samples}, built from tools/synth.py.

required.description: Characters every shipped language needs from the face.

compose.description: Character → [base glyph, mark glyph, "above" or "below", alias characters…] to compose when missing.

faces.description: More faces under the same license (an upright beside an italic), built with the same required, compose and dropSpaceKerning.

noteFont.description: The note's font file (the headline's when absent).

palette.description: light/dark → {paper, ink, accent, accentText} hex colors.

canvases.description: An Android canvas's [width, height] when not the default: android-phone 1080 × 1920, android-tablet 2560 × 1600 (store-screenshots.py --canvas; Google Play's limits still apply).

screens.description: screens.py: the same screens captured on every platform and shown side by side.

out.description: Captures, sheets and baselines (build/screens); keep it git-ignored.

platforms.description: Platform name (its folder under out) → how it's captured, in sheet order.

label.description: The name on the sheets (the platform name).

script.description: mac: the screenshot script, relative to the root, with screenshots.sh's options (Laching's).

vm.description: windows: vm.sh check-layout, every language side by side (the default), or vm.sh screenshots once per language, for a script without -Only.

device.description: ios: the simulator's device type, by name or identifier.

avd.description: android: the Android Virtual Device's name (avdmanager list avd).

orientation.description: The sheet's row: landscape on top (mac, windows), portrait below (ios, android). android: the emulator's screen is turned to it, auto-rotate off.

posture.description: android: a foldable AVD's posture for the run (the emulator console's `posture`).

crop.description: Crop each shot to its window: the transparent or flat margin around it goes.

list.description: Screen name → {platform name or capture kind → its shot: a name, {shot, env} or null}. A platform's own name wins over its kind; a platform with neither, or null, doesn't have the screen.

env.description: ios: more launch environment for this shot; android: more intent extras (LACHING_SCREENSHOT_MODE names the app's mode, "screens" when absent).

camera.description: android: the shot needs the front camera, so the emulator gets the host's webcam (-camera-front webcam0).

tool.description: The landing page's build command (vp, npm).

store.description: The store listing and what tools/store pushes (check.py, push.py, import.py).

dir.description: The listing folder: one <lang>.md per language in languages.all.

siteUrl.description: The landing page (privacy, support and marketing URLs); https://<domain> by default.

apple.description: App Store Connect (push.py). Paths are relative to store.dir unless noted.

appId.description: The app's Apple ID in App Store Connect.

releaseType.description: How an approved version is released: push.py sets it on an editable version of every platform. Without it, a version push.py creates is manual and an existing one keeps its own.

locales.description: Listing language → App Store Connect locale (en → en-US).

extraLocales.description: More App Store Connect locales a listing language fills when they exist (en → en-GB, en-CA).

baseTerritory.description: Where a new in-app purchase's price is set (ITA); USA by default.

iphoneScreenshots.description: <lang>/*.png per language, the iPhone 6.9" set; apple/iphone by default.

ipadScreenshots.description: <lang>/*.png per language, the iPad 13" set; apple/ipad by default.

duoScreenshots.description: <lang>/*.png per language, the iPhone Duo set (1398x2034 or 2007x2853); apple/duo by default. push.py's ios-screenshots part places them in the App Asset Library when the folder exists.

header.description: The iOS 27 product page header, one PNG for every language (3840x1646, no alpha); apple/header.png by default. push.py's ios-header part places it when the file exists.

searchResults.description: The iOS 27 search results asset, one PNG for every language (1920x1280 to 3840x2560, or 5244x2950, no alpha); apple/search-results.png by default. push.py's ios-search part places it when the file exists.

ios.description: A universal app's iPhone and iPad version page: the listing then has ios.promo, ios.keywords, ios.description and an optional ios.whatsnew (check.py), and push.py fills the iOS version too (--only ios-text,ios-screenshots).

iaps.description: The in-app purchases by product id; a missing one is created.

reference.description: The reference name in App Store Connect.

name.description: The listing field with its display name (apple.iap.supporter.name).

description.description: The listing field with its description.

reviewNote.description: The note for App Review; without one, App Store Connect's is left alone.

reviewShot.description: The App Review screenshot's file in review.shots; without one, App Store Connect's is left alone.

notes.description: The file with "## App Review Information → Notes"; app-review.md by default.

shots.description: The app's window captures, relative to the root (screenshots/macos).

google.description: Google Play; check.py requires the google.* fields of the listing when it's there, and store-screenshots.py knows Play's canvases.

screenshotCount.description: Screenshots (and captions) per language; 8 by default.

locales.description: Listing language → Play Console locale where it differs from the language (en → en-US, zh-Hans → zh-CN, nb → no-NO, pt-BR → pt-BR); the rest as Apple's.

microsoft.description: The Microsoft Store: the screenshots (store-screenshots.py --canvas microsoft), the Partner Center import (import.py) and submission (push-microsoft.py); check.py requires the ms.* fields when it's there.

art.description: poster-art.png, box-art.png, super-hero-art.png; microsoft/art by default.

publisher.description: The developer shown in the listing (DevStudio; devStudio in the submission API).

storeId.description: The app's Store ID in Partner Center (Product identity), which store/push-microsoft.py submits to.

shots.description: store-screenshots.py --canvas microsoft: the Windows captures (file names without .png, e.g. panel-light) in upload order, one per line of ms.captions (Partner Center takes up to 10); import.py and push-microsoft.py want this many screenshots and captions per language.

shadow.description: A hard shadow instead of the soft one: a block of the theme's color (#RRGGBB) behind each window, offset right and down.

offset.description: Pixels right and down; 16 by default.

backdrop.description: The canvas behind a light and a dark capture (#RRGGBB); the paper of screenshots.store.palette by default.

conform.description: companion.py conform: what the app keeps of its own on purpose.

allow.description: Files named like a Laching tool that are the app's own, not a copy of the tool (its own conformance.sh, say).

why.description: What it does that the tool doesn't.

verify.description: verify.sh: the app's own checks, run beside Laching's.

paths.description: An extended regular expression over the changed root-relative paths; the check runs when one matches (and with --all).

run.description: The command, run by bash from the app's root.

guardedExtra.description: More paths (regular expressions) agents must not edit by hand.

bigFileLines.description: A text file over this many lines may only be read by range (Read with offset/limit, sed -n 'A,Bp'), never whole; the hook says to read the outline first. Default 600; 0 disables.

longSessionTokens.description: The Stop hook tells the user once per compaction cycle when Claude's context is past this many tokens, so the next task goes to a fresh session. Default 130000; 0 disables.

guards.description: More guarded paths, each with the reason the agent is shown: never edited by hand, and with `reads`, never loaded either.

pattern.description: A regular expression over the root-relative path.

why.description: What to do instead, shown when the hook refuses.

reads.description: Refuse reads too (large or generated files); edits only by default.

slow.description: The app's slow checks, reminded at stop when a matching path changed since they last ran. A `name` of a built-in check (xcodebuild-test, conformance, swift-test, dotnet-test, dotnet-app-test, landing-build, winui-build, gradle-core-test, android-build) replaces its paths (and label); any other name adds a check, counted as run when a shell command matches `ran` (or a full verify.sh).

paths.description: A regular expression over root-relative paths.

label.description: How the reminder names the check.

ran.description: A regular expression over shell commands that run the check.

macUI.description: A path regex for Mac UI files; editing one reminds of the Windows twin.

windowsUI.description: The same for Windows UI files.

androidUI.description: The same for Android UI files; set, the reminder names Windows and Android.
